properties.name: Reviewed: gap:c628f709c27ad035
properties.rationale:
LEFT OPEN ON PURPOSE — Anthony's call 2026-07-31. The requirement is HIS OWN idea, captured the same day; accepting this gap parks the MODELLING question, not the intent.

WHAT BLOCKS IT IS A REAL VOCABULARY PROBLEM, FOUND BY CHECKING AND RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT. The first answer given was "reflow2 already has the vocabulary — model the release procedure as a Flow". THAT IS WRONG AS THE SCHEMA STANDS: PART_OF_FLOW is declared Capability -> Flow and accepts nothing else, so a Flow's steps must be Capabilities. "Bump the version in three files" is a chore, not a capability. Modelling seven release chores as seven Capabilities would put fake entries into the very set that coverage_report and the verification counts range over — 100 real capabilities plus seven chores makes every one of those reports quietly wrong, permanently. The correction is recorded here rather than edited over the earlier claim.

SO THE OPEN QUESTION IS ONE LEVEL DOWN, AND IT IS GENUINE: is a procedure step a first-class design object, or is it documentation the design POINTS AT? Making it first-class means widening PART_OF_FLOW to accept a step type — which MOVES THE STAMP and locks every older reflow2 out of the design, so it is a release-shaped decision, not a side edit. Pointing at it instead means writing the procedure as a document in the content store (which now exists) and referencing it from the Project — cheap, no schema change, but an agent reads prose rather than querying steps, which is most of what was asked for.

WHY NOT NOW: v0.20.0 was deliberately scoped to cap:changelog-view ALONE, and a schema change is not a side quest to slip in beside it. Nothing is lost by waiting — the requirement holds the reasoning and the derivability argument, and the seven recovered steps are written down outside the graph in the meantime.

THE ONE THING NOT TO DO is build it as a Flow of invented Capabilities to make this note go away. That would trade a visible open question for a silently wrong metric, which is the exact trade req:no-silent-fallback exists to forbid.

THE EVIDENCE STANDS AND IS NOT WEAKENED BY THE PARK: cutting v0.19.0 required reconstructing seven steps from `git show v0.18.0` plus a grep, and at least two of them — that an upgrade doc is owed ONLY when the schema stamp moves, and that the release manifest must be exhaustive with nothing computing it — were discoverable only from a past commit message.
